claim: The nightly export never writes the same order id twice, even when the feed repeats one. Either the dedupe step or the writer's seen-check catches it.
why: With the checked-in feed, main.py sorts by timestamp, so the two rows for order 7 end up with order 9 between them. The dedupe step only compares a row with the one just before it, so it keeps both. The writer's seen set is cleared after every batch of two, and the two copies fall into different batches, so it writes both and the output is [7, 9, 7].

deciding.note: seen set is cleared per batch

root.claim: The export never writes the same order id twice when the feed repeats one

atoms.evidence: It only compares a row with the previous kept row. main.py sorts by ts, which gives ids 7, 9, 7, so the repeats are not adjacent and both stay.

atoms.claim: The writer's seen set catches the repeated order
atoms.evidence: commit() clears the seen set after every batch of 2. The rows 7, 9 and 7 split into batches [7, 9] and [7], so the second 7 is written. main.py prints [7, 9, 7].
